court: Court of Appeals for the First Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction over petitions
issues.why: The court must confirm it has statutory jurisdiction to review the BIA orders and any issues raised.

issues.label: Final order for review
issues.why: The court must determine which BIA decision constitutes the final order after reconsideration and what remains reviewable.

issues.label: Effect of reconsideration grant
issues.why: Granting reconsideration may supersede the prior BIA decision and affect mootness or scope of the first petition.

issues.label: Timeliness of petitions
issues.why: The court must ensure each petition was filed within the statutory deadline and is not barred.

issues.label: Exhaustion of claims
issues.why: Only issues properly presented to the BIA are generally reviewable in the court of appeals.

issues.label: Waiver/forfeiture on review
issues.why: Arguments not developed in the opening brief may be deemed waived even if exhausted.

issues.label: Proper consolidation handling
issues.why: The court must ensure consolidation does not alter jurisdiction, scope, or remedies available.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (substantial evidence, abuse of discretion, de novo) to each type of determination.

issues.label: Review limits for discretionary asylum
issues.why: The court must identify which asylum determinations are discretionary and whether they are reviewable or barred.

issues.label: Legal vs factual questions
issues.why: The court must distinguish reviewable legal errors from unreviewable or deferentially reviewed factual findings.

issues.label: Due process claims preserved
issues.why: Any procedural fairness challenges must be assessed for exhaustion, prejudice, and legal sufficiency.

issues.label: Removal charge validity
issues.why: Although largely uncontested, the court may need to confirm the basis for removability is established and not legally defective.

issues.label: NTA and notice sufficiency
issues.why: Any challenge to the notice to appear or hearing notice can affect jurisdiction/validity if properly raised and preserved.

issues.label: Eligibility vs discretion split
issues.why: The court must separate eligibility findings from the IJ’s stated discretionary denial and assess both where relevant.

issues.label: Asylum one-year bar
issues.why: If implicated by the record, the court must confirm whether the asylum application was timely or excused, and reviewability limits apply.

issues.label: Credibility finding impact
issues.why: Because credibility was found, the court must ensure later analyses properly treated testimony as true absent contrary findings.

issues.label: Past persecution definition
issues.why: The court must assess whether the harm described legally qualifies as persecution under governing precedent.

issues.label: Protected ground identification
issues.why: The court must confirm the persecution was on account of a protected ground and not merely personal abuse.

issues.label: Family as social group
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether “family” is a cognizable particular social group under circuit/BIA law.

issues.label: Nexus to family membership
issues.why: The court must determine whether family membership was at least one central reason for the persecution.

issues.label: Alternative protected grounds
issues.why: The court must consider whether claims based on religion/political opinion/other PSG were raised and improperly ignored.

issues.label: Persecutor identity relevance
issues.why: The court must address whether harm by a parent and other Mungiki members constitutes private-actor persecution requiring state inability/unwillingness.

issues.label: State protection past harm
issues.why: For past persecution by non-state actors, the court must assess whether the record compels that Kenya was unable or unwilling to protect.

issues.label: Presumption from past persecution
issues.why: A past-persecution finding triggers a presumption of future persecution that the agency must properly apply.

issues.label: Burden on DHS for rebuttal
issues.why: The court must verify DHS bore the burden to rebut the presumption by a preponderance of the evidence.

issues.label: Fundamental change standard
issues.why: The court must assess whether the agency applied the correct legal standard for “fundamental change in circumstances.”

issues.label: Changed conditions evidence
issues.why: The court must review whether substantial evidence supports claimed improvements in Kenyan efforts against Mungiki.

issues.label: Individualized risk analysis
issues.why: Changed-conditions rebuttal must be tied to the applicant’s individualized risk, not only general conditions.

issues.label: Age/adulthood significance
issues.why: The court must assess whether adulthood alone can constitute a fundamental change and whether the agency reasoned adequately.

issues.label: Father control assumption
issues.why: The court must examine whether the conclusion that an adult is no longer at risk from a father is supported and considers ongoing threats.

issues.label: Non-father persecutors
issues.why: The court must ensure the agency properly accounted for risk from other Mungiki members, not just the father.

issues.label: Childhood persecution relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether the agency improperly discounted past persecution because it occurred in childhood.

issues.label: Internal relocation possibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether safe and reasonable internal relocation within Kenya rebuts fear and who bears the burden.

issues.label: Reasonableness of relocation
issues.why: Relocation analysis must consider practical, social, and safety factors, not just theoretical possibility.

issues.label: Future persecution probability
issues.why: If the presumption is rebutted, the court must consider whether the applicant nonetheless showed an independent well-founded fear.

issues.label: Pattern-or-practice claim
issues.why: If raised, the court must address whether there is a pattern or practice of persecution of the claimed group in Kenya.

issues.label: Objective/subjective fear
issues.why: The court must verify the agency properly assessed both subjective fear and objective reasonableness.

issues.label: Past persecution severity level
issues.why: For humanitarian asylum, the court must evaluate whether the severity of past persecution meets the “compelling reasons” threshold.

issues.label: Other serious harm prong
issues.why: Humanitarian asylum also requires assessing a reasonable possibility of other serious harm unrelated to protected grounds.

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum legal framework
issues.why: The court must confirm the agency applied 8 C.F.R. § 1208.13(b)(1)(iii) and relevant precedent (e.g., Matter of L-S-).

issues.label: Consideration of cumulative harm
issues.why: Severity and humanitarian determinations must consider cumulative harms and their long-term effects.

issues.label: Agency reasoning adequacy
issues.why: The court must ensure the IJ/BIA provided a reasoned explanation and addressed key evidence rather than conclusory statements.

issues.label: Discretionary asylum denial basis
issues.why: If discretion was invoked, the court must assess whether the agency relied on proper factors and supported adverse inferences.

issues.label: Law enforcement encounters weight
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the IJ’s reliance on U.S. law-enforcement encounters was lawful, supported, and properly balanced against equities.

issues.label: Discretion findings preserved
issues.why: The court must determine whether discretionary-denial grounds were adopted by the BIA and thus are properly before the court.

issues.label: Withholding legal standard
issues.why: The court must apply the “more likely than not/clear probability” standard and ensure the agency did not conflate it with asylum.

issues.label: Withholding not automatic denial
issues.why: The court must assess whether the IJ/BIA erred by treating asylum denial as necessarily precluding withholding without independent analysis.

issues.label: Withholding nexus standard
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the agency applied the correct nexus requirement for withholding (a reason, not one central reason, depending on circuit law).

issues.label: Withholding state protection
issues.why: For non-state persecutors, withholding also requires showing the government is unable or unwilling to protect, which must be analyzed for future harm.

issues.label: CAT legal definition of torture
issues.why: The court must ensure the agency applied the regulatory definition of torture (severity, intent, purpose, custody/control as relevant).

issues.label: CAT likelihood standard
issues.why: CAT requires “more likely than not,” and the court must verify the agency applied that standard to all asserted torture sources.

issues.label: Public official involvement
issues.why: CAT requires torture by or with consent/acquiescence of a public official, which must be correctly defined and applied.

issues.label: Acquiescence standard
issues.why: The court must assess whether the agency used the correct acquiescence standard (including willful blindness) rather than requiring direct intent.

issues.label: CAT individualized assessment
issues.why: The agency must consider the applicant’s specific risk, not only generalized conditions or past harm.

issues.label: CAT country-conditions use
issues.why: The court must examine whether the agency properly weighed country reports and other evidence regarding police conduct and Mungiki influence.

issues.label: CAT past harm relevance
issues.why: Past torture is relevant to CAT risk even if it occurred in childhood, and the court must ensure it was properly considered.

issues.label: BIA correction scope
issues.why: The court must assess whether, after acknowledging overlooked harms, the BIA adequately reconsidered the outcome rather than reaffirming without analysis.

issues.label: BIA reconsideration standard
issues.why: The court must confirm the BIA applied the proper standard for reconsideration (error of fact/law) and explained its decision.

issues.label: Harmless-error analysis
issues.why: If the agency erred (e.g., mischaracterized harms), the court must determine whether the error was harmless or prejudicial.

issues.label: Record-consideration duty
issues.why: The court must ensure the IJ/BIA considered all materially relevant evidence and did not ignore corroboration or key testimony.

issues.label: Corroboration requirements
issues.why: If corroboration was demanded or discounted, the court must evaluate compliance with corroboration rules and notice requirements.

issues.label: Persecution by Mungiki characterization
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Mungiki is treated as a gang/cult/religion and whether that affects protected-ground and nexus analysis.

issues.label: Mixed-motive persecution
issues.why: If motives include discipline/abuse plus protected grounds, the court must apply correct mixed-motive/nexus principles.

issues.label: Child applicant considerations
issues.why: Because harms occurred in childhood, the court must consider child-sensitive persecution analysis where relevant under precedent.

issues.label: Possibility of family-based retaliation
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether return could expose applicant to retaliation due to family ties or prior resistance to Mungiki involvement.

issues.label: Future harm by age mates
issues.why: The court must assess whether former “age mates” now adult Mungiki members pose ongoing risk despite the applicant’s adulthood.

issues.label: Government ability vs willingness
issues.why: The court must ensure the agency separately evaluated inability and unwillingness, not just general policing efforts.

issues.label: Selective enforcement/corruption
issues.why: Even with official efforts, corruption or local collusion can support inability/unwillingness or CAT acquiescence and must be considered if evidenced.

issues.label: Relief-specific remand scope
issues.why: If error is found as to one form of relief, the court must decide whether to remand for all related relief or only certain claims.

issues.label: Proper remedy on reversal
issues.why: The court must choose between granting relief, remanding for further factfinding, or affirming based on the appropriate appellate role.
